goal: measure serving-level (output-preserving) decode acceleration on real hardware
constraint: production GPUs shared; a benchmark model was served only in GPU1's free headroom (~25GB; production vLLM pre-allocates KV cache so free memory stays free) and torn down; production was not restarted or disrupted
measured_technique: fp8 weight quantization (online) vs bf16, same checkpoint
model: google/gemma-4-E4B-it (same family as the orchestrator; small enough to fit; note: MoE)

accuracy.verdict: fp8 is NOT automatically output-preserving here; it changed the extraction like the app-level tricks and needs the same regression validation. (E4B is MoE; fp8 on the dense gemma-31B may be more stable, but that was not measured.)

not_measured.speculative_decoding: output-IDENTICAL by construction, but the venv n-gram proposer is broken (numba needs NumPy <=2.2, venv has 2.4); the shared production venv was not modified
not_measured.tensor_parallelism: output-identical, but GPU0 is full with production; no second GPU free for a TP instance

conclusion: serving-level acceleration is real and measurable (fp8 +21-23% throughput), but it is not automatically accuracy-free: fp8 changed outputs. The truly output-lossless serving techniques (speculative decoding, tensor parallelism) preserve accuracy but require a maintenance window / spare GPU to measure, which this shared production environment did not allow.
